entries.title: Reconcile 'malformed hook response silently allows' with Cursor's documented block on invalid JSON

entries.rationale: editorial-judgment: The repo's headline Cursor safety fact contradicts Cursor's documented invalid-JSON-blocks behaviour. Splitting the two failure modes is a doc edit across three places. Keep the forum citation and add a probe; the deny design stays unchanged.

entries.title: Reconcile host-support.json gemini activation_gate 'none' with Gemini's untrusted-by-default project hooks

repo_claim.quote: "activation_gate": "none"

entries.proposal: Atlas shows Gemini treats project hooks (./.gemini/...) as untrusted by default and fingerprints them: a changed hook name or command is a new untrusted hook and warns before it runs. The installer writes project hooks into .gemini/settings.json, so an install or a pulled update can leave guardrails awaiting trust. Probe a live Gemini CLI first. If it prompts, set the gemini activation_gate to hash_trust (or a new value if the fingerprint covers only name and command), add a 'Hook trust' section to gemini-customization.md, and let _rc_rearm_notice print the re-trust reminder at install, update and status.
